signals.title: Iconic Viper V10 motorcycle temporarily moves home this winter
signals.summary: A team of volunteers have helped move the iconic Viper V10 motorcycle to the National Motorcycle Museum, where it will live this winter. After changing hands for the first time ever this summer, the Allen Millyard-built Viper V10 required up to seven volunteers to help move it to its ‘winter’ home. It was just over one month ago that Millyard watched the bike’s new owner, Tim Whittaker, ride the 500bhp machine for the first time. Of course, this was done under the guidance of Millyard, who knows every little detail about the bike after building it himself in 2009. Millyard owned the motorcycle, which features an 8.0-litre Dodge Viper V10 engine, until July 22, when it was sold at auction. The motorcycle changed ownership at the National Motorcycle Museum in Solihull, which is where it will live over the winter. Whittaker admitted at the time of buying the motorcycle that he intended to ride it frequently, as he did not want to see it stored in a collection. However, he also said that it would be loaned to the museum in the winter to allow visitors the chance to see the legendary motorcycle. Speaking in July, Whittaker said: “I didn’t want to see such an iconic motorcycle disappear into a private collection. It deserves to be ridden and enjoyed, and I’m looking forward to learning from Allen how to ride it properly. I’m incredibly proud to become its next custodian. Just as importantly, I’m delighted it will stay in the UK and that I can lend it to the National Motorcycle Museum during the winter months so visitors can continue to enjoy this remarkable machine.” Below is a video of the Viper V10 being carefully delivered to its ‘winter’ home, which required a team of volunteers to help move the motorcycle. A post shared by National Motorcycle Museum (@thenationalmotorcyclemuseum) The Viper V10 is considered one of the most iconic custom motorcycles ever built, however, Millyard is known for these types of projects, after also producing the ‘Flying Millyard’, which uses a 5,000cc V-twin engine derived from an air-cooled Pratt & Whitney R1340 aviation motor. signals.title: Paralysed motorcyclist sets new 200mph top speed record with Suzuki Hayabusa
signals.summary: Talan Skeels-Piggins has set a new land speed record for a paralysed motorcyclist, after blasting past 200mph on a turbocharged Suzuki Hayabusa. British biker Talan Skeels-Piggins has become the first paralysed motorcyclist to break the 200mph top speed barrier, ending an 11-year wait to achieve the new record. Skeels-Piggins achieved a top speed of 200.254mph on a turbocharged Suzuki Hayabusa, which was timed over a mile run at the Straightliners World Speed Record event. The British motorcyclist, who is a former Winter Paralympian, achieved the new land speed record at the Elvington Airfield outside of York, last month. A former downhill skier, Skeels-Piggins swapped the winter sports discipline for two-wheeled motorsport in 2012, where he became the first paraplegic rider in the world to compete against able-bodied motorcycle racers. Paralysed from the chest down since 2003, Skeels-Piggins set his new land speed record on the fifth attempt, after overcoming challenging weather conditions and high winds. The 200mph record marks the culmination of an 11-year journey that began in 2015, where Skeels-Piggins clocked a top speed of 175mph while riding a standard Hayabusa. At the time, this was a significant achievement, however, it was still short of the intended 200mph target. During the last 11 years, Skeels-Piggins has faced various setbacks and financial challenges, making his new 2026 world record all the more rewarding. The new record also comes one year after Skeels-Piggins began working with motorcycle engineer and racer Lee Baxendale. The pair decided to revive Skeels-Piggins’ project, which involved Baxendale devoting more than 600 hours to building, modifying, testing and preparing a turbocharged Suzuki Hayabusa. Speaking after setting the new record, Skeels-Piggins said: “I am extremely grateful to everyone who has played a part in this record attempt. We weren’t completely sure whether the runs would actually go ahead because of the weather, or what sort of speed we would reach, but to get to 200mph is incredible. “The bike ran well, and both my crew and the Straightliners team were professional and hugely supportive. Without them, this would not have happened.” Find the latest motorcycle news on Visordown Your information will be used in accordance with our Privacy Policy . signals.title: Honda launches a new scrambler motorcycle concept in China
signals.summary: Honda used the CIMA motorcycle trade show in Chongqing, China, to reveal a new retro-inspired scrambler concept. Honda has revealed an all-new CB250SS retro-themed scrambler motorcycle, although we might have to wait a while before it lands in the UK. At the heart of the new model is a 249cc liquid-cooled engine, however, the Japanese brand has not yet revealed power and torque figures. What we have noticed about the new scrambler concept is that it’s tailored towards riding on the road, thanks in large part to its road-biased footpegs, 17-inch alloy wheels front and back, as well as a short-travel suspension system. With Honda keeping information, and images of the CB250SS to a minimum, the photos shared by the company don’t do the bike, nor its colours justice. The bike features a dark brown seat resting on top a navy-coloured under-fairing section, while the fuel tank features a mix of white and red colours, both of which are found on the small fairing at the front, too. The forks are finished in gold, offering a premium feel aboard the new scrambler concept, while a round TFT display with Honda RoadSync connectivity is believed to be part of the setup. The new CB250SS scrambler, although a concept model at this stage, appears destined for production. A production version is expected to be launched in China some time in 2027, before being offered in other markets. Honda has not confirmed where the CB250SS will be produced, but it is unlikely to arrive in the UK in its current guise. That being said, bringing the new CB250SS to the UK could be a very smart move from Honda, given the popularity of the GB350S. A post shared by Peak Motorcycles (@peakmotorcycles) The latter has become one of the most adored modern classic motorcycles across the UK over the last two years, therefore, a CB250SS scrambler could potentially find similar success. signals.title: CCM’s last remaining stock surprisingly appears at UK auction
signals.summary: After closing its doors in June 2025, CCM Motorcycles’ last remaining stock is going up for auction in the UK. Founded back in 1971, Bolton-based CCM Motorcycles , which closed its doors in June 2025, still has brand-new stock that can be purchased in the UK. But these particular bikes have not gone up for sale where you might have expected them to, with Gateway Auctions instead making them available as part of a UK-based auction. This comes after the auction house purchased the remaining CCM Motorcycle fleet when the company collapsed last year. A collection of 10 brand-new CCM motorcycles will be available, although this is not expected to be the final auction involving some of its stock. According to reports, a final auction could take place sometime next spring, subject to the remaining models clearing the Motorcycle Single Vehicle Approval (MSVA) process, which allows a motorcycle to be registered on the road. Alongside the 10 motorcycles set to go under the hammer this week, a wide selection of factory-built spare parts, workshop equipment, and even memorabilia, will be available. The motorcycle collection features everything from CCM bobbers, scramblers, a roadster, flat tracker, and even a CCM Spitfire Moto R. Bidding can only be done online, however, the Lancashire-based auction house will be hosting a public viewing on Tuesday, October 13. The auction currently features a total of 1,504 lots, including various banners and signs, paddock stands, seats, fuel tanks, and much more. You can find out more about the lots included on the official Gateway Auctions website , while the auction is set to end on Thursday, October 15. CCM Motorcycles was founded by motocross rider and engineer Alan Clews, and was in operation for over 50 years. Prior to its collapse, things seemed to be on the up for the British brand, after it secured a major investment from Pitalia Capital, led by entrepreneur Anil Pitalia. However, extension into international markets, and the launch of a new retro adventure bike called, Project X, both of which were planned, never materialised. signals.title: New motorcycle sales show two-wheel sector is crucial to UK’s transport system
signals.summary: New motorcycle registrations are continuing to grow across the UK, leading to the MCIA repeating its call for government action on the rider licensing and training review. So far in 2026, motorcycle registrations have climbed by 14.8 per cent across the UK compared to the same period in 2025, highlighting why industry bodies are pushing for the government to make the two-wheel sector a bigger priority in its transport system. Across the entire year to date, total registrations have grown by 14.4 per cent, which includes all vehicles under the wider L-Category umbrella, such as mopeds, scooters, motorcycles, and more. 87,685 L-Category vehicles have been sold compared to 76,649 at the same stage in 2025, according to the Motorcycle Industry Association (MCIA). The motorcycle sector has, unsurprisingly, been the driving force behind the improved numbers, with adventure bikes responsible for the biggest year-to-date rise. New adventure motorcycle registrations have grown by 23.4 per cent so far this year, with competition bikes a close second at 22.5 per cent. For the month of September, the total market grew by 6.8 per cent vs the same month last year. Bike sales in the competition segment increased by 27.1 per cent for the month, which was highest of any motorcycle category. The best-selling brand was Honda , which was the only manufacturer that sold over 2,000 units. The Japanese company sold a total of 2,159 units in the UK, while BMW and Triumph managed to break past the 1,000 unit mark, with 1,256 (BMW) and 1,001 (Triumph) sales respectively. Speaking about the continued growth, Tony Campbell, CEO of MCIA, said: “September is a key month for the full year market being the second largest of the year, so it is very pleasing to see the market continue to recover from 2025.” Campbell also went on to address the ongoing rider license and training review, where he repeated his call for the government to respond favourably towards motorcyclists. Campbell started by saying “mopeds, motorcycles and other L-Category vehicles should be a key element in a well thought out integrated travel system where [the] government needs to work harder to fully understand what the solutions are.” “As this Government moves forward with devolution and reindustrialisation, it needs to recognise that this sector is about much more than getting from A to B. It also supports manufacturing, innovation, skilled jobs and social mobility and that’s why we’re committed to working with ministers on smarter, integrated travel policies and urge the government to respond positively as it considers the review of rider licensing and training”. signals.title: Neumeister shuts down rumours of KTM production moving to India
signals.summary: After recently turning profit for the first time in nearly two years, KTM CEO Gottfried Neumeister has shut down rumours suggesting the company’s production could be moved from Mattighofen. KTM CEO Gottfried Neumeister has confirmed production of the Austrian manufacturer’s motorcycles will continue to take place at its headquarters in Mattighofen, Austria. This is in response to recent rumours suggesting KTM’s motorcycle production could be moved to India. Following 18 months of turmoil for the Austrian brand, which started around this time in 2024, recent months have looked a lot better for the company. KTM recently turned profit for the first time in nearly two years, while the company sold nearly 100,000 motorcycles in the first half of 2026. This marks a drastic turnaround from where the Austrian marque was just 12 months ago, where major debt had piled up, hundreds of employees were let go, and creditors, along with current owners Bajaj Auto, stepped in to save the company. But KTM is now back on track in terms of the wider outlook for the brand, as well as its MotoGP project, which has been renewed for another five years. However, convincing Bajaj that its MotoGP, and wider motorsport programmes were worth continuing, did not come easy when the Indian company initially took over KTM in 2025. Speaking to Speedweek.com , Neumeister said: “At the start, there was little understanding of motorsport. They come from the world of commuters, where sales are driven by price; there, different attributes are important than here. It took me several trips to India to convince them. We couldn’t have made our commitment to MotoGP for the next five years without their backing. “I’ve been given the go-ahead from the top to set up an independent team, so Bajaj hasn’t taken over the management. There were also rumours that production would be moved to India, but there is a clear commitment to Austria. We have over 440 engineers who design top-class products and set new standards.” While KTM has regained a foothold in the two-wheel sector, there is still work to be done after the financial struggles it endured during the last two years. That will continue over the coming months, with the manufacturer keen to re-position itself as one of the leading brands globally, but especially in Europe. “When I look at the market around us, the other European manufacturers are posting losses in the first half of the year. Of course, everyone is now saying that we’re coming from a lower base; nevertheless, it’s very encouraging that we’re outperforming the market and have sold almost 100,000 motorbikes. “Volume isn’t everything; we must first become profitable before we can scale up the business. We’re on the right track, and all our new products are being well received. The company’s future depends on this.” Find the latest motorcycle news on Visordown Your information will be used in accordance with our Privacy Policy . signals.title: Watch: Michael Dunlop fires up special Gilera 250 GP bike
signals.summary: Michael Dunlop has teased the possibility of the Isle of Man TT record holder riding a special Marco Simoncelli-liveried Gilera 250 GP bike. As far as iconic race bikes and road racing legends go, it doesn’t get much better than a special Marco Simoncelli-liveried Gilera 250 GP machine and TT record holder Michael Dunlop. But that’s what we have here, courtesy of a social media post from the 36-time Isle of Man TT winner. Dunlop’s post includes pictures and a video of him with the Simoncelli-liveried Gilera 250 GP bike, as well as a caption that reads: “Now for something special”. Of course, this could all be harmless wording from the road racing legend, who moved ahead of his father's total of 135 Irish road racing wins in the summer. However, it does suggest Dunlop could be thinking of racing the bike in the future. This has not been confirmed by the Ballymoney rider, so it remains to be seen whether that happens or not. In the video shared by Dunlop, which is part of a separate post from the one featuring pictures of him and the GP bike, the Northern Irishman can be seen firing up the Gilera 250, which also has slick tyres fitted. The Metis Gilera 250 GP bike was raced by Simoncelli in the 250cc class from 2006 to 2009, before the popular Italian moved up to MotoGP with the San Carlo Honda Gresini team in 2010. Simoncelli, who raced with the now iconic number 58, tragically lost his life in 2011 when he crashed at the Malaysian Grand Prix, at Sepang. Simoncelli fell into the path of Valentino Rossi and Colin Edwards, and ultimately passed away due to his injuries. Whether Dunlop was to race the GP bike, or simply ride it in a non-competitive setting, it would be a fitting tribute to the Italian nonetheless, who was tipped as a future MotoGP world champion before his accident. signals.title: This is the outcome when timeless motorcycle culture meets contemporary design
signals.summary: Royal Enfield has teamed up with premium British helmet maker Hedon, and the result is 16 limited-edition helmets split evenly into two different styles. Royal Enfield has announced a new collaboration with premium British helmet maker Hedon, which includes a limited-edition run of 16 helmets, aimed at bringing together timeless motorcycle culture, contemporary design and uncompromising craftsmanship. Royal Enfield, which specialises in small-to-mid displacement motorcycles, is set to enter a busy period with the rollout of its first 750cc machines expected soon. The Indian-owned company will reveal a brand-new Himalayan 750 and Continental GT 750, with the former potentially set to be unveiled at next month’s EICMA show in Milan, Italy. But before that happens, customers have the chance to buy one of these premium Royal Enfield x Hedon helmets, which are inspired by the latter’s ‘Hedonist and Heroine Racer’ styles. The exclusive collection features eight half-face and eight full-face helmets, all of which will be handcrafted to order. Available globally, the new collection is aimed at modern classic and retro motorcyclists in particular, as well as collectors. According to Royal Enfield, “the collaboration is a coming together of classic motorcycles, sartorial style and a shared passion for the culture of motorcycling. The resulting collection is designed for discerning riders and collectors who appreciate the finer details – from core motorcycle enthusiasts to fashion-forward riders”. Now, in order to buy one of these two helmets, customers will need to spend a considerable amount of their hard earned money. That’s because the ‘Hedonist Royal Enfield’ helmet, which is the half-face option, will cost £1,650. Meanwhile, those looking for a cafe racer style can buy the ‘Heroine Racer 2.0 Royal Enfield’ helmet for £2,100. Both helmets meet ECE 22.06 and DOT safety standards, and are available in sizes ranging from small to XXL (half-face option) and small to XXXL (full-face lid). signals.summary: 作为目前国内市场首款双缸中排休旅踏板，新车精准填补了国产中大排休旅踏板的品类空白，凭借全新双缸动力、行业首发智能电控技术以及全场景休旅配置，为长途通勤、摩旅用户带来全新选择，也进一步完善了赛科龙休旅踏板产品矩阵。 最关键的动力层面，RT450搭载全新398cc并列同步双缸水冷发动机，最大功率31.5kW，最大扭矩44.2N·m，动力参数领跑同级单缸车型。 为了得到更好的骑行质感，赛科龙在发动机内部大做文章，包括内置平衡轴、主副平衡齿、活塞背冷等多项核心优化结构，不仅可以全转速区间的稳定平顺输出，且可有效解决传统单缸踏板高速震动明显的短板。双缸结构带来的高密度点火输出，也让整车动力响应更灵敏、运行质感更细腻，兼顾城市代步的平顺性与高速巡航的动力储备。 其中IPDU智能电源管理系统采用全新芯片集成架构，替代传统零散电路元件，具备毫秒级故障防护、智能诊断、自动重试修复能力，支持一键封车超低功耗静置，搭配手机APP全域电气状态监测，大幅提升整车电路稳定性。 同步搭载的EHS能量采集系统，配备高转化率柔性太阳能板，支持行车双源补能、静置持续蓄能双重模式，有效提升整车充电效率，抵消车辆静态功耗与电瓶自放电损耗，显著延长电池使用寿命，降低用户长期养护成本，解决了摩托车闲置亏电的普遍用车难题。 智能化和舒适性配置上，RT450主打全域豪华体验，全系搭载FEELFUN非凡智能系统。整车配备77GHz毫米波雷达、盲区监测、后方碰撞预警、前后高清行车记录仪及哨兵模式。搭配智能光语系统、弯道辅助照明、紧急爆闪灯等安全配置，全方位提升骑行安全性。 交互层面支持落座感应、NFC刷卡、蓝牙感应、APP远程四重解锁，搭配可投屏语音控制的TFT全彩仪表、自适应电动风挡、电动折叠后视镜、电加热手把与坐垫，全面覆盖全季节、全场景骑行需求。 针对休旅骑行场景，新车进行了专项底盘与实用性优化。整车采用高强度双摇篮车架与HSC操稳系统，搭配前西互、后日清专业制动卡钳、玛吉斯半热熔轮胎、气囊可调双后减震，另外标配双通道ABS+TCS，底盘稳定性、滤震舒适性与制动安全性全面拉满。 同时配备的18L大容量油箱可以提供400km+的续航、可容纳双全盔的超大座桶空间更是实用，适配长途摩旅、日常通勤、多人出行等多元用车场景。 RT450的信息其实也并不是什么秘密了，今年摩博会赛科龙不仅亮相了RT450，还提供了试驾，并且在赛科龙的第四季“大国风光”中进行了4000公里的新疆极限试炼，现在新车终于正式上市，感兴趣的车友们可以行动啦！

signals.title: 骑行热身，从“手”开始
signals.summary: 秋风一起，气温骤降。对于每一位骑士来说，秋冬季节骑行最让人头疼的，往往不是身上的寒风，而是那一双最先“投降”的手。手指僵硬、反应迟钝，不仅影响操控，更关乎安全。 维多利亚Sixties系列深谙骑士所需，全系标配三段式可调手把加热功能，用一份从掌心蔓延至全身的温暖，重新定义秋冬骑行的舒适边界。 Sixties系列的手把加热开关按键集成在左侧把手上，位置符合骑行直觉，触手可及。骑行途中无需低头寻找，手指轻按即可完成温度切换，真正做到“盲操”无障碍。 手把加热的核心优势在于“快速暖手” 。相比佩戴厚重手套后仍难抵严寒的被动方案，电加热手把直接从握把内部发热，热量均匀传导至掌心与指腹，且无需额外充电、无需担心手套臃肿影响操控手感，是秋冬骑行更为高效、可靠的暖手方案。 对于大多数骑士而言，秋冬骑行的高频场景是日常通勤。清晨出门时气温往往只有个位数，骑车到公司的路上，冷风从袖口灌入，手指在几分钟内就变得僵硬。 有了Sixties的手把加热，通勤路上的体验截然不同。上车、启动、轻按加热开关，几乎在出发的同时，掌心已经开始感受到温度。一路骑行到目的地，双手始终保持着灵活的操控状态，不必再为“到了公司手指冻得打不了卡”而烦恼。 如果说城市通勤是手把加热的“日常场景”，那么在高原、高海拔等极端环境下，它就从“舒适配置”升级为 “保命配置” 。 我们的车友@笑着好看 对此深有体会。他在长途摩旅中，选择骑行维多利亚Sixties 150Si+ 穿越阿里地区。那是平均海拔5000米以上的无人区，天气瞬息万变——出发时还是阴天，转眼间大雪与冰雹交替袭来，气温骤降至零下。 在这种极端条件下，手指如果被冻僵，捏刹车、拧油门的精准度都会大打折扣，安全风险成倍增加。好在Sixties 150Si+ 的手把加热功能全程在线，三档温度调到最高，掌心始终保持着可感知的温暖。 高原摩旅的经验告诉我们，手把加热在恶劣环境中的价值远不止“舒服”二字。它直接关系到操控安全！手指灵活，才能及时应对突发路况；掌心温暖，才能在漫长的无人区骑行中保持专注和体力 维多利亚Sixties系列以三段式可调手把加热这样看似“小”的配置，解决的是每一位骑士在寒冷天气中真实面临的“大”问题。无论是城市通勤的清晨与傍晚，还是高原长途的冰雪与狂风，它都在那里，默默守护着你的双手，也守护着你的骑行安全。

signals.title: EICMA 2026: ALWAYS LIKE THE FIRST TIME, BUT NEVER THIS BIG
signals.summary: From November 3 to 8, Fiera Milano Rho will host the 83rd edition of the International Motorcycle Exhibition. Highlights include MotoGP, the Dakar, legendary champions, test rides and live shows. EICMA 2026 will be the largest edition ever held at Fiera Milano Rho. Presented in Milan, the event will occupy ten exhibition halls for the first time, covering more than 300,000 square metres, with 754 exhibitors and 2,120 brands from 52 countries . International brands account for 74% of the total, while approximately 30% of direct exhibitors are newcomers or returning participants. “Always the first time. Every year, a new discovery” is the slogan chosen for the 83rd edition, which also aims to enhance the visitor experience through larger spaces and a new layout for the exhibition's various attractions. From MotoGP to the Dakar: all the highlights One of the main attractions will be the debut of Speed Legends , an exhibition dedicated to the history of MotoGP. Hall 22 will showcase more than 30 historic motorcycles, alongside the five leading bikes of the 2026 season. The partnership with MotoGP will also bring simulators, interactive content and opportunities to win exclusive experiences at Misano and Mugello. The Dakar will also return to Hall 22, featuring historic and modern motorcycles, as well as an official container dedicated to interactive content. In the outdoor area, MotoLive will host off-road races, Freestyle Motocross, Acrobatic Trial, music with Radio Deejay and free test rides. Special guest Toni Bou will be in attendance. The programme will also include races featuring twin-cylinder motorcycles from 20 manufacturers and the Champions Charity Race Legend , with Troy Bayliss, Marco Melandri, Stefan Everts and other champions. The races will also be broadcast on Sky. Also returning are Y.U.M. , offering more than 40 electric and internal combustion vehicles to test, EICMA Adventouring , dedicated to adventure motorcycling and events organised through the FMI circuit, and the start-up area , supported by ICE and focused on innovation. To make travelling to the event easier, EICMA will provide approximately 15,000 free parking spaces from November 6 to 8 , alongside initiatives with ATM, Trenord and BusForFun to encourage the use of public transport. The exhibition will run from November 3 to 8, with the first two days reserved for the press and industry professionals. The event will be open to the public from November 5 to 8, from 9:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. Online tickets start at €20 for a full-price ticket and €10 for a reduced ticket , plus booking fees. Afternoon tickets, valid from 1:30 p.m., will also be available, starting at €14 . signals.title: T.ur Garda Hydroscud: the two-layer jacket for mid-season riding
signals.summary: In Autumn and Spring, when conditions on two wheels can change from morning to night, wearing a jacket capable of adapting to shifting temperatures and standing up to rain is essential . To deliver the right level of comfort, T.ur’s Garda Hydroscud relies on a two-layer construction. Water protection is guaranteed by the fixed Hydroscud membrane—100% waterproof and breathable, with a 10,000 mm water column rating and 7,000 g/m²/24h breathability. The outer shell is made of Polystrong 600D with Pro-Shell inserts, both treated with Drop Safe water-repellent finish for extra protection against the elements. When temperatures drop, the 100g removable thermal lining (thermal rating 3 out of 5) provides the necessary warmth. When the sun comes out, Airflow System vents on the sleeves ensure proper ventilation. The styling emphasizes practicality: a total-black look with red accents on the sides and shoulder blades, adjustments at the forearms and hem, and four pockets. Certified EN 17092:2020 Class A, the Garda Hydroscud is equipped as standard with CPS Level 2 armor on the shoulders and elbows, and is prepared for Easyflex 3in1 Back Armour or Comfort back protectors (both Level 2). High-visibility reflective inserts further enhance rider safety. The new jacket is available now in sizes ranging from S to 4XL. signals.title: Honda Gold Wing: both versions receive a refreshed colour lineup
signals.summary: After celebrating the 50th anniversary of the presentation of the first-generation model in 2025, the Honda Gold Wing aims to confirm its position as a benchmark in the Luxury Tourer segment. Without introducing any new technical solutions, for model year 2027 Honda has completely renewed the colour range for both versions currently available, the standard model with a Bagger profile and the Tour. The latter features richer equipment, including, among other things, a 61-litre top box with integrated speakers, heated seat and airbag, as well as a larger windscreen. The 2027 standard version is available exclusively in the new Gunmetal Black Metallic. As for the more imposing Gold Wing Tour, customers can choose from three new colour schemes, all of them previously unavailable. The options are Iridium Gray Metallic, Graphite Black and Allumage Blue Metallic. The current model is the sixth-generation Honda Gold Wing, launched in 2017 and powered by a formidable 1.8-litre six-cylinder boxer engine, paired with a seven-speed DCT automatic transmission. On the Tour version only, a conventional six-speed manual transmission is also available.
